name: Quasar J0529-4351
citation: Wolf C. et al. (2024) The accretion of a solar mass per day by a 17-billion solar mass black hole. Nature Astronomy 8, 520
notes: Most luminous known quasar: close to its Eddington limit

name: GW150914 merger (peak)
citation: Abbott B.P. et al. (2016) Observation of gravitational waves from a binary black hole merger. PRL 116, 061102

name: Human body at rest
citation: Henry C.J.K. (2005) Basal metabolic rate studies in humans: measurement and development of new equations. Public Health Nutr 8, 1133

name: World-class track cyclist (peak)
citation: Dorel S. et al. (2005) Torque and power-velocity relationships in cycling: relevance to track sprint performance in world-class cyclists. Int J Sports Med 26, 739
notes: Pmax 1600 +/- 116 W for a few seconds; body mass approximate

name: Earth's internal heat flow
citation: Davies J.H. & Davies D.R. (2010) Earth's surface heat flux. Solid Earth 1, 5

name: Jupiter's internal heat
citation: Li L. et al. (2018) Less absorbed solar energy and more internal heat for Jupiter. Nat Commun 9, 3709
notes: 7.485 W/m2 over the whole planet (computed): Jupiter is still cooling from its formation

name: Crab pulsar spin-down
citation: Hester J.J. (2008) The Crab Nebula: an astrophysical chimera. ARA&A 46, 127
notes: 5e38 erg/s drawn from the neutron star's rotation powers the whole nebula

name: R136a1 (most massive known star)
citation: Crowther P.A. et al. (2010) The R136 star cluster hosts several stars whose individual masses greatly exceed the accepted 150 Msun stellar mass limit. MNRAS 408, 731
notes: 265 Msun and nearly 9 million suns: right at its Eddington limit (later estimates are somewhat lower)
